About us

Founded in 2015, B2C2 is a global leader for institutional liquidity within digital assets. We bring 24/7 365 days a year deep, reliable pricing for spot, futures, options, CFDs, and NDFs across all market conditions. Our growing team has deep expertise across pricing, structuring, risk, systems, and regulation.

B2C2 bridges the gap between traditional financial and digital assets, and is relied upon by brokerages, exchanges, banks, fund managers, and other institutions to provide 24/7 liquidity. Headquartered in London, with global offices in Paris, Jersey City, Tokyo, Singapore, and Luxembourg, our fast-growing team has expertise in traditional financial and crypto markets.

We pride ourselves on our company culture and ability to attract not only the top talent but the right people. If you are looking for a role in an exciting new industry, at a dynamic company please keep reading.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Engage clients and counterparties to help facilitate the Client KYC/Onboarding and Client Lifecycle processes such as initial KYC, periodic and ad-hoc reviews
  • Coordinate client / counterparty KYC onboarding across multiple functions / B2C2 entities - Front Office, Compliance, AML, Operations, Legal, Risk, amongst others – all in a high pressure / time-sensitive environment
  • Assist in ongoing monitoring, banking enquiries, other KYC related matters, as and when required
  • Ensure all departmental requests are completed within expected timeframes
  • Ensure that client maintenance activities are acted upon in a timely manner
  • Review agreements, legal and financial documents, and other paperwork for completeness and accuracy
  • Assist in the assessment / assignment of risk classifications to incoming clients / counterparties and those expanding / changing business activities; where applicable, adjust KYC profiles due to changes in risk factors
  • Undertake recertifications and renewal of due diligence on existing clients / counterparties to ensure identification of changes in risk profile, including reputational and operational risk factors
  • Participate in design and testing of enhancements to client due diligence / onboarding databases, reports, and systems
  • Support management in its tactical / strategic initiatives regarding onboarding applications / other systems
  • Work closely with Sales, Compliance, Legal and other teams to render policies / procedures more transparent and effective, all while preserving risk control strength

Required Skills and experience:

  • KYC/Client onboarding experience
  • Appreciation for due diligence operations and onboarding applications / systems
  • Strong interpersonal skills: Effective communicator both written and verbal
  • Ability to face-off to management team, Front Office, Sales, Compliance, Legal, Audit
  • Well-organized and good at multitasking. Track-record of keeping good composure in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment
  • Understanding of US PATRIOT Act, BSA / AML requirements (e.g. CIP
    requirements; difference between CDD and EDD; etc), Dodd-Frank, 5MLD, MLR 2017, MLR 2019 among others
  • High competency in research and analysis, and in using external due-diligence
  • Energetic / self-starter. Ability to take direction and act quickly
  • Healthy mix of compliance and pragmatism / commerciality in an environment where revenue growth is a mandate and risk control is paramount
  • High competency in Google products suite and interest in AI technology enhancement

A strong culture is a common denominator among the most successful companies and B2C2 is proud to be a values-based company.

  • Ambitious - Striving to make history through world class achievements
  • Innovative - Forward looking in our solutions for clients and employees
  • Meritocratic - Rewarding positive contribution across the organisation
  • Collegiate - Achieving through teamwork through a healthy environment
  • Risk Aware – Informed decision making and considered in our practices

B2C2 is committed to a policy of equal employment opportunity for applicants and employees and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds. As such, B2C2 will not tolerate discrimination against any of our employees on the basis of membership in a protected category. We are also committed to creating an inclusive environment to ensure we attract, engage, promote and retain the best talent. We will consider flexible working arrangements for any of our roles.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. 

The Workplace Operations team ensures Robinhood offices run smoothly each day, supporting employees through reliable services, well-maintained spaces, and engaging workplace programs. The team partners closely with IT, Recruiting, People Operations, and Finance to deliver consistent, high-quality office experiences across locations. Day to day, that means clear service standards, quick follow-through on requests, and regular check-ins with vendors and partners. Team members focus on operational excellence, strong service standards, and creating environments where employees can do their best work!

As a Campus Operations Manager, you will manage daily office operations in our headquarters in Menlo Park, CA and serve as a key point of contact for employees, vendors, and building management. You will oversee workplace services such as supplies, maintenance, and office programs while supporting events and onboarding activities. This role contributes to a welcoming, organized, and productive environment by maintaining high standards across facilities and services. You will also support office projects and coordinate with internal partners to ensure consistent workplace practices across locations.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA office, with in-person attendance expected 5 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Proven ability to independently manage projects, prioritize competing demands, and take ownership of initiatives from planning through execution.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to identify opportunities, recommend solutions, and follow through on results.
  • Experience coordinating employee events, workplace programs, and initiatives with teams across the company.
  • Excellent organizational, communication, and time management skills, with strong attention to detail.

Mysten Labs’ mission is to advance the internet through step-function improvements in what technology makes possible. We build foundational infrastructure and products that give people, businesses, and developers new ways to interact, transact, and create value.

Our work spans on-chain finance and the emerging agent economy. Through Sui, Move, and our broader technology stack, we’re building the systems that make these experiences possible - from secure, scalable blockchain infrastructure to new ways for businesses and AI agents to interact.

About Mysten Labs

Through Sui and our financial products, we’re building infrastructure and experiences for trading, liquidity, and asset management. Alongside that work, we’re developing the infrastructure and products AI agents need to operate reliably, handle sensitive information, and interact under clear rules.

As agents take on more responsibility, they need more than intelligence. They need persistent context, trusted access to information, and clear boundaries around what they can do. Mysten brings together capabilities across storage, memory, privacy, and policy-controlled interactions to help make that future possible.

The Role

We’re hiring a Product Lead to turn our emerging agentic technologies into products customers can understand, adopt, and buy.

Your role is to translate our product capabilities into useful experiences and commercially viable offerings—for example, a commerce-focused product that helps retailers manage agent-driven shopping, returns, or refunds.

Working closely with our CTO, Sales Lead, and engineering, you’ll identify customer problems, rapidly prototype solutions, and help bring the strongest opportunities to market. You’ll connect customer discovery, product definition, experience design, and commercialization, staying close to the work from the first concept through launch.

Joining this team means helping define a new product category, its customer experience, and the business around it. You’ll have the opportunity to shape how businesses participate in the agent economy and bring that vision to market.

What You’ll Do

  • Identify and prioritize customer problems our other agentic products are well positioned to solve.

  • Lead customer discovery alongside our CTO, developing a clear understanding of buyer needs, user workflows, and adoption barriers.

  • Rapidly create prototypes, interactive demonstrations, and product variants using AI-assisted design and coding tools.

  • Test concepts with customers and use their feedback to refine the experience, scope, and value proposition.

  • Define product requirements and work with engineering to turn validated prototypes into reliable, production-ready offerings.

  • Shape packaging, pricing hypotheses, positioning, and GTM strategy in partnership with sales and the broader team.

  • Design experiences that make agent capabilities, permissions, policies, and human oversight understandable to users.

  • Balance customer-specific needs with opportunities to build reusable capabilities and repeatable products.

  • Define success measures across customer value, adoption, conversion, and revenue, using results to guide iteration.

What You’ll Bring

  • 12+ years of Product Management, Product Design, or related experience

  • A track record of taking new products from an ambiguous opportunity through customer validation, launch, and commercial adoption.

  • Startup or similarly entrepreneurial experience, with direct ownership of building and shipping under uncertainty.

  • Strong prototyping skills and hands-on experience using AI-assisted or agentic coding tools to build and iterate on functional experiences.

  • Experience working directly with customers to define products, validate demand, and support pilots or sales conversations.

  • Commercial judgment, including experience contributing to packaging, pricing, positioning, or GTM decisions.

  • Strong UX instincts and the ability to make complex technology approachable without obscuring important controls or constraints.

  • Enough technical fluency to collaborate with engineering on integrations, feasibility, and the path from prototype to production.

  • A hands-on working style and the ability to influence across product, design, engineering, and sales.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with customer-facing AI, enterprise commerce, payments, trust and security, or workflow products.

  • Experience with agent permissions, approval flows, auditability, or other mechanisms that help businesses control automated actions.

Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which may include verification of employment history, education credentials, criminal history, and other relevant information.

Regarding the recent rash of technology job scams: Be aware that emails from genuine Mysten Labs group recruiters will always come from the @mystenlabs.com domain or related subdomains (e.g., mystenlabs.com/careers). Remember: you can always verify positions on our job boards at www.mystenlabs.com/careers.

To support an efficient and fair hiring process, we may use technology-assisted tools, including artificial intelligence (AI), to help identify and evaluate candidates. All hiring decisions are ultimately made by human reviewers.

Our team is remote first and we are hiring across the world. Here at Mysten Labs, you’ll be joining a world-class team with tremendous growth potential as we bring the next billion users to web3. We raised a $300M Series B round from top Silicon Valley led venture funds like Jump Crypto, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Binance Labs, Redpoint, Lightspeed, Coinbase Ventures, Electric Capital, Standard Crypto, NFX, Slow Ventures, Scribble Ventures, Samsung Next, Lux Capital, among other investment firms and strategic partners. Come join us and build the future of web3!

descriptions.job-0hh84jg:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

The impact you'll have

We're looking for a Group Product Manager who understands that this role is not coordination — it's ownership. This is a player-coach role: you'll lead and develop the Product Managers who own Onchain Compliance, and you'll personally drive the most important initiatives in the portfolio. You're accountable for what your team ships and for the caliber of the PMs who ship it.

You'll own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for TRM's Onchain Compliance products, serving financial institutions, fintechs, crypto businesses, and regulators, and the outcomes your team delivers: adoption, retention, and ARR.

  • Leading: Hire, coach, and develop PMs. Give direct feedback, know each PM's growth areas, and step in early when a PM or project starts to slip.

  • Setting direction: Set the vision for onchain compliance and prioritize across your PMs. Define success and failure with real metrics.

  • Staying hands-on: Own a few critical initiatives yourself. Prototype, build AI agents, and ship alongside your team.

  • Closing: Build ongoing customer relationships and join strategic deals. Turn what you hear into roadmap unlocks.

  • Reporting and risk: Tell leadership how Onchain Compliance is doing, using real metrics. Call out risks early and unblock PMs before projects fail.

What we're looking for

Core product skills

  • Product ownership: You own outcomes, not coordination. You've taken complex enterprise products from discovery through launch to measurable business impact.

  • AI-native execution: You already build agents and use AI to accelerate your work and your team's. You can demo it.

  • Bias for action: You make decisions with incomplete information and ship working solutions in days, not weeks.

  • Product taste: You know what great looks like, and you make opinionated calls on what to build, what to cut, and when to ship.

Leadership skills

  • People leadership: You've built and grown a team of PMs, not just inherited one. You can point to a PM whose performance changed because of something you did.

  • Vision and communication: You simplify complex ideas, align teams around what matters, and inspire others to build toward a shared vision.

  • Metrics-driven: You define success and failure with real metrics, report honestly on how things are going, and call out risks early.

  • Cross-team influence: You set expectations and unblock work with PMs and teams outside your own.

  • Commercial ownership: You build direct customer relationships, understand financial and regulatory workflows, and answer for adoption, retention, and revenue.

The following represents the expected range of compensation for this role:

  • Individual pay is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. The compensation details listed in this posting reflect the US base salary only.

  • The estimated base salary range for this role is $230,000 - $245,000.

  • Additionally, this role may be eligible to participate in TRM’s equity plan.

  • Please note – we factor in the different costs for geographies outside the United States.

     

Our R&D team is distributed not distant and will participate in work weeks, typically 1–2 times per quarter, at a TRM hub or other designated location. Work weeks may be scheduled with as little as 14 days’ notice, and some roles may require additional travel based on team and cross-functional needs. TRM coordinates and covers approved travel, lodging, and workspace. Accommodations are available for legitimate caregiving, health, immigration, and similar

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com.

To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form.

Recruitment agencies

Own Your Intelligence

 

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

 

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

 

Prime Intellect has raised $150M in total funding from Founders Fund, Radical Ventures, NVIDIA, and exceptional AI, infrastructure, and enterprise operators — including Andrej Karpathy, Dwarkesh Patel, and leaders and founders from Ramp, Perplexity, Harvey, Mercor, Zapier, Datadog, Cognition, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Together AI, SemiAnalysis, LangChain, Browserbase, Cloudflare, Sierra, Databricks, Airbnb, OpenRouter, Standard Intelligence, Fleet, Core Auto, and more. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.

Role Impact

You will own applied RL programs from the first ambiguous customer problem through a deployed improvement loop. You will understand the workflow and business stakes, decide what can be measured and learned, build the environment and evaluation, run post-training experiments, deploy the result, and determine what should generalize into Prime's shared stack. The majority of your work will be organized around external programs. You will work directly with customer researchers, engineers, and leaders, and you will be accountable for both the research result and its practical impact.

Responsibilities

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Role scope

We have active programs across technology, science, engineering, regulated industries, and the public sector.

Representative early problems

  • Turn a partially documented workflow and business goal into an environment, baseline, and evaluation that the customer team agrees measures the right outcome.

  • Improve a domain agent through RL or another post-training method while separating model limitations from task, harness, inference, and integration failures.

  • Carry a successful experiment into deployment, measure its effect on the customer outcome, and convert the recurring parts into reusable environments, recipes, data loops, or platform capabilities.

What you will own

  • Technical and business discovery that produces a clear research plan, success measure, environment, and baseline.

  • RL, distillation, and other post-training experiments tied to deployment outcomes.

  • Agent systems that handle tool use, memory, recovery, long horizons, and human oversight.

  • Deployment and adoption decisions, plus reusable artifacts carried back to Prime's research, engineering, and product teams.

Requirements

  • Relevant experience: customer-embedded technical work, research engineering, technical founding experience, applied ML consulting with real build ownership, or end-to-end post-training programs.

  • You should be comfortable with senior external teams and able to connect experimental evidence to business decisions without lowering the research bar.

  • Hands-on experience building and debugging model-training, post-training, agent, evaluation, or closely adjacent experimental loops.

  • Strong experimental judgment: meaningful baselines, careful trace inspection, clear failure attribution, and a willingness to change direction when the evidence changes.

  • Strong Python and the ability to build artifacts that other researchers and engineers can run, inspect, and extend.

  • Comfort owning ambiguous problems and keeping partners and teammates current as you resolve them.

Evidence of exceptional work

We value publications, open-source systems, benchmarks, and shipped products as evidence of exceptional work. Show us something difficult you built, what failed, and how the evidence changed your approach.

Benefits and Perks

  • Cash Compensation Range of $150-300k + equity incentives

  • Flexible Work (San Francisco, New York, London, or remote)

  • Visa Sponsorship & relocation support

  • Professional Development budget

  • Team Off-sites & conference attendance

If you're excited about the opportunity to build the foundation for the future of decentralized AI and create a platform that empowers developers and researchers to push the boundaries of what's possible, we'd love to hear from you.

Founded in Silicon Valley in 2009 by Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, Andreessen Horowitz (aka a16z) is a venture capital firm that backs bold entrepreneurs building the future through technology. We are stage agnostic. We invest in seed to venture to growth-stage technology companies, across AI, bio + healthcare, consumer, crypto, enterprise, fintech, games, and companies building toward American dynamism. a16z has $100B+ under management across multiple funds.

We’ve established a team that is defined by respect for the entrepreneur and the company-building process; we know what it’s like to be in the founder’s shoes. We’ve invested in companies like Anduril, Airbnb, Coinbase, Cursor, Databricks, Deel, Figma, GitHub, Roblox, SpaceX, and Stripe. Our team is at the forefront of new technology, helping founders and their companies impact and change the world.

The Role

We're hiring a Lead Engineer, Incident Response to lead and shape a16z's detection and response team. This is a hands-on role: you'll spend a significant portion of your time investigating incidents, writing and reviewing detections, building automation, and making the harder technical response decisions. You'll also manage and develop the engineers on the team.

You'll build and improve detection and response capabilities across the firm's cloud, SaaS, identity, and endpoint environments, shaping the roadmap, tooling, threat hunting, and response practices. You'll also develop capabilities to protect the firm against impersonation and fraud. You'll work closely with Security Engineering, IT, Legal, Compliance, and other cross-functional teams to put these capabilities into practice and turn lessons from incidents into better detections, tooling, and controls.

Venture capital firms face threats that extend beyond their infrastructure: capital call wire fraud, impersonation, and social engineering against employees and partners, alongside attacks by organized criminal and nation-state groups. Your work protects sensitive firm and limited partner (LP) information, financial transactions, and the relationships the firm depends on.

This role requires an in-office presence 2 days a week in our San Francisco, CA office.

To join our team, you should be excited to: 

  • Set the detection and response roadmap, prioritizing the threats that matter most to the firm and measuring detection coverage, alert quality, and response effectiveness
  • Lead and develop engineers through coaching, feedback, performance management, and technical reviews, working alongside them on investigations and engineering projects
  • Develop the team's ability to respond from triage through containment, eradication, and recovery, including vendor incidents. Lead major incidents, coordinate a16z's technical response with system owners and affected providers, and escalate decisions requiring leadership or Legal approval
  • Maintain and test response playbooks and escalation criteria through cross-functional tabletop exercises and incident simulations
  • Design and improve SIEM architecture and security logging with Security Engineering and IT, expanding detection coverage across cloud, identity, and endpoint environments, including EDR. Write, review, test, and tune detections as code, using relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques to assess coverage and working with system owners to close visibility gaps
  • Run hypothesis-driven threat hunts informed by threat intelligence and prior investigations, turning findings into new detections
  • Build and improve brand protection capabilities including monitoring, investigation, and takedowns of lookalike domains, fraudulent websites, and social media accounts
  • Build AI-assisted response automation. Evaluate accuracy and reliability before deployment and define where human judgment and approvals are required
  • Keep technical and non-technical stakeholders aligned during incidents, including IT, Legal, Compliance, Finance, and investing teams. Clearly communicate impact, uncertainty, response options, and next steps
  • Develop the team's postmortem practices, lead reviews of root causes and contributing factors, and drive corrective actions to completion with the teams responsible for remediation
  • Participate in the Security team's on-call rotation

Minimum Qualifications

  • 9+ years of incident response or detection and response experience, or equivalent demonstrated impact, with depth in cloud incident response across AWS and GCP
  • Prior experience managing security engineers, including coaching and performance management, while remaining technically hands-on
  • A track record of building and leading detection and response programs, making architecture and prioritization decisions, and delivering measurable improvements
  • Experience leading high-stakes incidents across cloud, SaaS, identity, and endpoint environments, including forensic investigation, containment, recovery, and postmortems
  • Strong detection engineering skills, including SIEM query languages or rule formats such as KQL or Sigma, detection-as-code, testing, and tuning

  • Experience running hypothesis-driven threat hunts and investigating sophisticated attacks, including identity compromise, social engineering, and data exfiltration
  • Strong Python skills and experience building and reviewing maintainable security automation
  • Working knowledge of AI and agent systems, including their limitations and security risks when used in triage and response workflows
  • Experience leading cross-functional security work and communicating incident impact, uncertainty, and technical trade-offs clearly to non-technical stakeholders and senior leaders
  • Sound judgment under pressure, balancing security risk and business impact and recognizing when to escalate
  • Low ego, high empathy, and a track record of effective collaboration across teams

GCIH or an equivalent incident response certification is a bonus but not required.

Role Overview

The Customer Success Manager is a hands-on player-coach who owns the external link with our Ethena Pay users. You'll be the single accountable owner of the customer experience after signup. On day one you'll be in the queue answering tickets yourself, including the hard ones. For the 1st 6 months, expect roughly 70% doing the work and 30% building the operations of the function. You’ll be the 1st, so there is huge potential career growth baked in here. You’ll find your maximum ability and seniority level within the team, as the need for a larger support and payments ops org grows around you.

Support is a key place a money product can truly stand out, and few competitors set a high bar We want users to tell other people how good our support is, and we want ticket volume to fall because the reasons for them are being removed. You'll sit directly inside the product team, working closely with Engineering, Finance, Compliance, and our GTM team.

Role Responsibilities

  • Own the queue personally: handle most inbound tickets yourself early on, own Zendesk end to end (triage, tagging, macros, help centre). You’ll publish, and hold yourself to, the first response and resolution targets.

  • Set a support quality bar users talk about: define what best-in-class looks like in writing, measure satisfaction and public sentiment properly, run response QA, and contact affected users before they contact us.

  • Turn support into measured input for product and engineering: a standing weekly read by cluster and contact rate, every defect routed with impact and an owner, and clear escalation thresholds so emergencies move fast and routine volume never interrupts engineering.

  • Automate the work: remove the causes of the largest clusters through product fixes, self-serve answers and automated status updates, use AI-assisted triage with a human check wherever money is involved, and track falling effort per user as an explicit goal.

  • Be the named operational owner of our rails vendors (card issuer, on/off-ramp, KYC and wallet partners), with escalation paths, a vendor incident log and evidence for commercial reviews.

  • Bring the manual money workflows under documented control: runbooks, four-eyes checks and audit trails for reconciliation, disputes and chargebacks, refunds, stuck withdrawals, fraud triage and KYC edge cases, working with parent Finance and Compliance.

  • Build and lead the operations function: bring support across the ticket queue, Telegram and X into one operation, own user-facing incident comms, run an operations KPI dashboard, and grow a small front line and payments-ops team toward follow-the-sun and multilingual coverage.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Previously run support or operations for a live consumer money product where mistakes moved, lost or delayed real customer funds, such as a neobank, payments company, card program, exchange or crypto money app.

  • Owned operational KPIs and reported them regularly to executive and product audiences, with examples of numbers you moved and how you moved them.

  • A track record of reducing the work, not just absorbing it: contact rates brought down or clusters engineered out, with before-and-after numbers.

  • A support experience you built that users praised, backed by satisfaction or sentiment data.

descriptions.job-019br7g:
Why this role exists

Our web experience is a company asset, owned and managed by marketing. It is a strategic growth platform and our most effective engine for brand, demand, customer engagement and education, and revenue.

We are hiring a Web Strategy and Execution Lead to run it that way. This is not a website management role. It is an ownership role for a commercial platform, accountable for what the asset returns to the business.

You will set the strategy for how our web estate earns attention, converts intent, educates customers, and contributes pipeline and revenue. You will then build, test, and ship against that strategy on a permanent cycle.

Primary accountability

Increase the commercial contribution of our web estate through strategy, customer experience, conversion optimization, content, search, technology, and continuous experimentation.

What you will own

Web strategy and development

  • Own the strategy and roadmap for our web estate, tied directly to commercial outcomes rather than page count or release volume.
  • Define what the platform is for by audience and stage, from first exposure through evaluation, purchase, onboarding, and ongoing customer engagement.
  • Make the case for investment with a clear view of cost, return, and opportunity cost. Prioritize ruthlessly and be willing to retire what does not perform.
  • Build the operating rhythm: intake, prioritization, delivery, measurement, and iteration.

Conversion and growth

  • Own conversion performance end to end, from traffic quality through to qualified pipeline and revenue contribution.
  • Run a continuous experimentation program with a live hypothesis backlog, clear success criteria, and honest read-outs on what did not work.
  • Optimize the full journey rather than isolated pages: entry points, navigation, forms, demo and trial flows, self-serve routes, and handoffs to sales and e-commerce.
  • Partner with demand generation on campaign landing experiences, personalization, and lead quality.

Content and search

  • Own the search strategy across search engine optimization (SEO), answer engine optimization (AEO), and generative engine optimization (GEO), so we are found and cited in traditional search and in AI-generated answers.
  • Build the technical, structural, and content foundations that support discoverability at scale: information architecture, schema, site performance, internal linking, and content governance.
  • Work with brand, product marketing, and content to turn our domain expertise into web content that ranks, converts, and holds up to scrutiny from a compliance audience.
  • Track share of visibility against the categories we intend to lead.

User experience and customer experience

  • Be the advocate for the user inside the business. Know the journeys, the friction, and the drop-off points, and be able to evidence all three.
  • Run continuous research and feedback loops: session analysis, user testing, surveys, and direct customer input.
  • Raise the quality bar on usability, accessibility, and performance across every device and market we serve.
  • Extend the experience beyond acquisition into onboarding, education, and existing-customer engagement.

Technology and execution

  • Own the web technology stack and the roadmap for it, including content management, testing and personalization tooling, analytics, and the integrations that connect web to our marketing and revenue systems.
  • Make build, buy, and partner decisions with a clear view of speed, cost, and long-term maintainability.
  • Manage agency and contractor relationships where we use them, and hold them to the same standards we hold ourselves to.
  • Work with information technology (IT), security, and data teams on privacy, consent, resilience, and compliance requirements.

Data and measurement

  • Define the measurement framework for the asset: the metrics that matter, how they connect to pipeline and revenue, and how we report them.
  • Build the instrumentation and attribution needed to make that framework trustworthy, in partnership with marketing operations and data.
  • Turn analysis into decisions. Every significant change should have a hypothesis behind it and a read-out after it.
  • Give the wider business a clear, regular view of how the platform is performing commercially.

Who you will work with

This role sits at the center of the marketing organization and reaches across the company.

  • Marketing leadership. Align the web roadmap to the overall marketing strategy and investment case.
  • Product marketing. Translate positioning, messaging, and launches into web experiences that convert.
  • Demand generation. Deliver the conversion layer for campaigns, and improve lead quality as well as lead volume.
  • Brand. Protect and build the brand experience online, and grow our share of visibility in the categories we want to own.
  • Product. Connect the marketing site to the product experience, including trials, self-serve, and in-product education.
  • Sales. Understand what turns web interest into qualified conversations, and close the gap between the two.
  • Customer success. Extend the platform into customer education, engagement, and retention.
  • People. Support the employer brand and the candidate experience on our careers pages.
  • IT and data. Keep the stack secure, compliant, well-integrated, and well-instrumented.

What you will bring

  • Significant experience owning a commercial web estate in a business-to-business (B2B) technology, software as a service (SaaS), or FinTech environment.
  • A track record of measurable commercial improvement: conversion rate, pipeline contribution, revenue, or self-serve growth, with the numbers to evidence it.
  • Depth across conversion rate optimization and experimentation, including how to design a test, size an opportunity, and interpret a result honestly.
  • Strong command of search in its current form, including how AI-driven answer engines are changing discovery and what that means for content and technical strategy.
  • Fluency with modern web technology and analytics, enough to make good architecture and tooling decisions and to hold technical partners to account.
  • Experience leading through influence across marketing, product, sales, and engineering stakeholders.
  • Comfort operating as both the strategist and the person who ships.

How you will work

  • Innovative and future thinking. You look ahead of the current playbook and are already testing what comes next.
  • Commercially minded. You think in return on investment, not activity, and can defend your priorities in commercial terms.
  • Customer obsessed. You start with the user, and you can describe their journey in detail because you have watched it.
  • Data driven. You form hypotheses, test them, and change your mind when the evidence says so.
  • A strong strategic thinker. You can hold a two-year view of the platform and explain it clearly.
  • An excellent executor. Strategy without shipping does not count. You move quickly and finish things.
  • Influential. You bring stakeholders with you without needing authority over them.
  • Growth minded. You seek feedback, share credit, and treat failed tests as information rather than embarrassment.
  • Permanently experimental. The site is never finished, and you would not want it to be.

We especially like people who are obsessed by users, journeys, hypotheses, experiments, prioritization, conversion, data, and outcomes.

What success looks like in the first year

  • A clear, funded, and agreed strategy for the web estate, with the commercial case behind it.
  • A measurement framework the business trusts, and regular reporting against it.
  • A live experimentation program with a consistent cadence and documented learnings.
  • Demonstrable improvement in conversion and commercial contribution against an agreed baseline.
  • Improved visibility in both traditional search and AI-generated answers for our priority categories.

Benefits

About us

Luno is the crypto investment app you can rely on, enabling you to buy, store and explore crypto securely. We’re committed to putting the power of cryptocurrency in everyone's hands, sensibly and responsibly. Since 2013, we’ve helped millions of people around the world invest safely in crypto. All products and cryptocurrencies on our platform must first meet stringent legal, risk and technical security standards.Transparency is key for us. We're available in multiple markets around the world and we work closely with regulators and other key stakeholders to ensure compliance with local laws, as we believe this is the best way to help everyone, everywhere, invest safely.

The role in a nutshell:

This is a senior role with management and strategic responsibility for the success of Luno's global OTC desks, reporting to the Head of Treasury. You'll manage OTC principal traders across several markets, ensuring that they act within defined limits at all times and you’ll ensure that flow from institutions, corporates and professional traders is profitably traded on a risk-adjusted basis. Sitting within our Treasury team, you'll work with the heads of our Stablecoin and Payment / Remittances initiatives, in-country teams and relationship managers to turn that flow into a consistently profitable book.

Your mission will be: 

Team management

  • Manage and mentor a team of traders, fostering a culture of high performance, risk awareness, and commercial proactivity.
  • Ensure that trading activity is within defined strategies, counterparty credit limits, operating limits and allocated working capital.
  • Ensure that trade disputes are cleanly managed by Traders, stepping in where required.
  • Ensure that Trade execution and Trade Settlements are per Standard Operating procedures.
  • Ensure that accurate records of trades and P&L are kept.

Manage P/L and risk

  • Own the aggregate of desk's P&L and risk-adjusted P/L against targets and risk limits — you'll know your numbers cold and be able to defend every line of them.
  • Manage the execution of trades to hedge Luno's market risk on its working capital and revenue streams, and execute revenue liquidation trades.

Manage trading strategy

  • Agree trading strategies across multiple desks relating to crypto and FX — for OTC, corporate hedging and revenue liquidation. Develop and agree strategies for derivatives, arbitrage and warehousing as the desk matures — always with risk management and profitability at the core.

Reporting responsibility

  • Aggregate reporting at the Global level, for regular distribution to senior stakeholders on trading activity, performance and market insight.

Build the desk

  • Motivate for changes in counterparty credit limits, operating limits and allocated working capital, where required to support sustainable profitability.

  • Pressure-test our risk frameworks and models, and make the case for changes as market dynamics shift.

Relationship management

  • Establish and nurture internal relationships with Cross functional teams across Luno (Marketing, Sales, Product, Compliance, Legal etc).
  • Build durable relationships with desk clients alongside our traders, country teams and relationship managers — the goal is repeat flow, not one-off tickets.

descriptions.job-020druk:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About Production Engineering

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

  • One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

  • If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

  • We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

  • We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

  • We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

Our Teams

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across four areas:

  • Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale

  • Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

  • Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture

  • Developer Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs

What You'll Do

Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure. You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team.

As a Tech Lead & Manager, you are a hands-on player-coach: you will lead and grow a team while remaining directly engaged in the technical work. Management at Ramp does not mean stepping away from the technology or the code. You will help set direction, develop engineers, and work alongside the team to deliver consequential infrastructure outcomes.

Day to day, you will:

  • Build, coach, and grow a high-performing team. Create clarity, give direct feedback, mentor engineers, and help each person expand their technical judgment, ownership, and leadership.

  • Set technical direction for your team’s domain. Identify the highest-leverage problems, define a path forward, bring the right people along, and stay engaged with the team until the work is delivered.

  • Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale.

  • Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved.

  • Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time.

  • Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs.

  • Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers.

  • Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE.

  • Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom.

  • Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done.

What We Look For

We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team.

The mindset we're looking for:

  • You love building teams, mentoring engineers, and helping people grow—and you are equally energized by writing code, reviewing designs, and digging into complex distributed systems.

  • You are a true player-coach. You know when to coach, delegate, and create space for others to lead; you also know when your direct technical involvement will create the most leverage.

  • You can set a technical direction, bring people along, and then lock in with the team to make it happen.

  • You do not believe managing engineers means stepping away from the technology or the code.

  • You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem.

  • You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job.

  • You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right.

  • You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win.

  • You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one.

  • You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am.

Experience profile:

  • Experience managing, mentoring, and developing engineers. You create clarity, give direct feedback, and help people grow in technical judgment, scope, and leadership.

  • Track record of delivering through cross-functional coordination: aligning stakeholders, unblocking teams, and staying accountable for the outcome.

  • Comfortable using AI tooling and coding agents as part of your everyday engineering workflow — and helping a team use them to move faster and think bigger.

Bonus (not required):

BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, financial institutions, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit www.bitgo.com.

This role will require being full-time onsite at our Palo Alto office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving.

BitGo is looking for a design leader who still designs. You will manage and mentor the design team, own the design system, and sit next to the Chief Product Officer on business strategy.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it literally. You will carry your own design surfaces and ship them, alongside leading the team. Expect roughly 50% hands-on IC work to start, decreasing as the team scales. It will not go to zero — the person setting the craft bar should be practicing at it.

We are not a design-forward company today. We intend to become one, and we want you to lead that shift.

The team you will lead

The design team is small, senior, and self-sufficient. Each designer owns a wide vertical outright — trading, staking, DeFi vaults, earn, wallets, financing — with deep product context and strong opinions about the work. They are running at capacity, which is part of why this role carries real IC load: you will pick up the retail mobile experience and design system rather than distributing that work across a team that is already full.

What they have asked for is specific, and we are hiring against it: a leader who gets into the work early with product and engineering rather than arriving at the end, who can critique craft because they still practice it, who tells them plainly what the next level requires, and who gives the team air cover so they can do the deep work instead of patching to hit dates.

What you will own

  • Your own design work. You will own surfaces directly and ship them at the quality bar you are asking of everyone else. Discovery through spec, in Figma, in the reviews, on the hard problems.
  • The team's growth. Invest in each designer individually. Be explicit about what the next level requires and give people the work that gets them there. Feedback should be candid, specific, and about the craft. Respect the ownership designers already have — autonomy is how this team works best, and your job is to raise the ceiling, not take the pen.
  • Design's standing in the company. Amplify the team's visibility, voice, and strategic impact. Represent design in strategy, roadmap, and architecture conversations, and push for the client experience when nobody else in the room will.
  • Upstream involvement. Join product and engineering at discovery, not at handoff. Shape long-term roadmaps with PMs so the team builds toward a direction instead of absorbing late changes.
  • The design system. Own the system and component library end to end: tokens, patterns, governance, contribution model, and adoption across product teams. Translate company strategy into a system flexible enough that teams ship scalable experiences rather than one-off patches.
  • Systems design. Our platform spans seven product areas with shared primitives — accounts, wallets, assets, entitlements, approvals. Design the system, not the screen.
  • The discipline. Establish UX and systems thinking as a practice the whole organization runs on, not a stage a design team owns. Product managers, engineers, and business leads should be able to frame a client problem, map the system it lives in, and evaluate a solution against real client needs. That is how we ship value to every client type we serve, in every market we operate in — rather than a set of features that work for the loudest account.
  • How we work. Establish the processes a small team needs to move fast without losing quality: critique, documentation, design review, and clean handoffs with engineering. Set the quality bar and hold it, including for AI-assisted work.
  • Technical depth. Read a technical design, understand the constraint, and decide with engineering where to compromise, where to hold, and where a broader change is worth the cost. Get into the mechanics with the team on the hard edge cases — the crypto ones and the design ones.
  • The face of design. Be present and known internally, and represent BitGo design externally with clients, partners, and candidates.

What success looks like

By six months: the design system has a clear owner, a versioned component library, and measurable adoption. Product teams stop reinventing patterns. You have shipped design work of your own that the team points to as the standard. Every designer knows what their next level requires and has work that supports getting there.

By 12 months: design is in the room early on strategy, not late on execution. Product and engineering partners frame problems in client terms without being asked. The team has grown in size and capability. At least one flagship surface has shipped with a coherent, systemized experience clients notice.

Who you are

  • Experience leading design in financial services. Digital assets, or another domain of genuinely complex technical flows, strongly preferred.
  • You have built and owned a design system at scale, not just used one.
  • Hands-on in Figma and a role model for craft. You are shipping design work today, not describing work you shipped four years ago. You can sit in a critique and give feedback that is specific enough to act on.
  • Deep in UX. Strong product thinking, logical reasoning, and decisions grounded in data rather than taste alone.
  • You have managed designers and made them better. You care about how the team is doing, not only what it ships.
  • Technically literate. Comfortable with APIs, data models, and engineering trade-offs.
  • Direct communicator. You can hold a position with a Chief Product Officer, an engineering lead, or a client, and change your mind when the argument is better.
  • You want the mandate. Turning a technical, compliance-heavy platform into a design-led one is the appeal, not the obstacle.

Helpful, not required

  • Regulated environments: broker-dealer, trust company, bank, or qualified custodian.
  • Experience with complex permissioning, approval workflows, or multi-entity account structures.
  • Design leadership at a company that went through the same shift you would lead here.

Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Join a team of great people who strive for excellence and personify our corporate values of ownership, craftsmanship, and open communication. We are looking for new colleagues who bring innovative ways of thinking and problem-solving, and who want risks to be part of the team that changes the world’s financial markets.

  • 100% company-paid health insurance for employee, partner, and dependents

  • Free custom lunches and snacks

Depending upon your leveling and location, the compensation for this role averages between $210,000 and $250,000 USD base salary. Equity, an annual performance bonus, and the benefits outlined above are also part of this role’s package.

About Us

Established in 2018, Bybit is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency exchanges and digital financial platforms, serving over 80 million users across more than 200 countries and regions. Powered by world-class technology and a user-first mindset, Bybit delivers a seamless ecosystem across trading, payments, wealth management, custody, institutional services, and Web3 — connecting users to the future of digital finance.
 
Our core values define how we build. We listen, care and improve to create products and experiences that put users first. Backed by a global team of ambitious builders, problem-solvers, and innovators, we foster a high-performance and fast-moving environment where talent is empowered to drive real impact at the global scale. Supported by 24/7 multilingual customer service and a strong commitment to innovation, we are shaping the future of finance through technology, collaboration, and bold execution.
 
Today, Bybit is recognized as one of the most trusted and transparent platforms in the digital asset industry, continuing to expand its global presence while building the infrastructure for the next generation of financial services.
 
Role Summary
We are looking for a sharp, operationally minded AML professional to sit within our second line of defence function. This role exists to bridge the gap between regulatory expectation and operational reality: you will hold deep AML/CTF subject matter expertise and use it to systematically identify where processes fall short — through inefficiency, control gaps, or design flaws — and drive them to a measurably better state. You will challenge the first line with authority, propose solutions with precision, and own the outcome.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Map and critically assess existing AML/CTF processes end-to-end — CDD, transaction monitoring, screening, SAR, ongoing due diligence — identifying inefficiencies, control weaknesses, duplication, and regulatory exposure.
  • Translate findings into structured, prioritised improvement proposals with clear risk rationale, implementation path, ownership, and measurable success criteria.
  • Challenge first-line operational teams constructively but rigorously; hold them accountable to regulatory standards and internal policy without becoming an operational bottleneck.
  • Act as internal subject matter authority on AML/CTF regulatory requirements and Global best practices; ensure process design decisions are grounded in current regulatory expectation.
  • Track implementation of agreed process improvements through to completion; monitor whether changes deliver the intended effect and escalate where they do not.
  • Support regulatory examinations, internal audits, and third-line reviews by providing clear, well-evidenced process documentation and subject matter input.
  • Contribute to the AFC risk assessment cycle by surfacing process-level control gaps as input to the overall AML/CTF risk picture.
What You Bring
  • 7+ years of hands-on AML/CTF experience, with significant exposure to both operational (1LoD) and oversight (2LoD) environments — you understand how processes actually run, not just how they are documented.
  • Demonstrable track record of identifying process failures and driving material, measurable improvements in an AML or compliance context.
  • Strong working knowledge of AMLD IV/V/VI, FATF Recommendations and EBA AML/CTF Guidelines.
  • Structured analytical approach: able to decompose a complex process, identify the critical failure point, and communicate it clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Credible and direct: comfortable challenging senior stakeholders and first-line management with evidence-based positions.
  • Experience in a regulated payments, crypto-asset, or fintech environment preferred.
  • CAMS, ICA Diploma, or equivalent AML qualification an advantage.
What Good Looks Like in This Role
  • Processes you review come out measurably more efficient, better controlled, and more defensible to a regulator than when you found them.
  • The first line treats your findings as valuable input, not bureaucratic overhead — because your recommendations are specific, practical, and grounded in operational reality.
  • When the regulator or internal audit asks how a process works and why it is designed that way, there is a clear, documented answer that traces back to your work.

Why Join Us
At Bybit, we are committed to fostering a supportive and enriching work environment. 
Our benefits include:
- Study Growth Fund: We support your professional development and continuous learning.
- Internal Events: Participate in regular team-building activities, workshops, and events designed to promote collaboration and innovation.
- Global Collaboration: Be part of a diverse, international team, working alongside colleagues from around the world.
- Career Advancement: Access opportunities for growth and advancement within a rapidly expanding global company.
- Internal Mobility: Grow with us- Your long-term development is important to us. We offer internal job opportunities to help build your career path.
